messages.subject: categorical exogenous variables and significance
parts:
I'm a graduate student in ecology, and I'm building a SEM for modeling species distributions, with various environmental variables as factors. However, I'm new to SEM and lavaan, and am slightly confused by the inclusion of categorical variables

 

I have 4 different canyons which I sampled from, with multiple sites within the each canyon. Given that these canyons are disparate geographically, though somewhat homogeneous within, I wanted to include canyon as a categorical variable, modeling the effect of species dispersion. 

 

Given that canyon is an exogenous variable, from my understanding, I created 3 different dummy variables for the 4 canyons, populated by 0s and 1s, to delineate which canyon it is (like in classical regression). My first question is: is this the appropriate thing to do? 

 

Secondly, when building this model, I have all three canyon variables as factors controlling other variables.  Below is the code for part of my base model. Right now I’m trying to trim down the model. From what I understand, I want to eliminate non-significant paths. However, with my categorical variables, what happens if two of the three are considered non-significant? Do I throw just those part of the canyon variable out of the model? In thinking back to classical regression, this doesn’t entirely feel right: rather, it seems like I should just keep them all in, unless they are all non-significant. Thought?

  

 

model<- '

N~CanM + CanR + CanSC

P~CanM + CanR + CanSC

Tan~CanM + CanR + CanSC

Avg~CanM + CanR + CanSC

Dist~ Aspect + Avg +N + P + Tan + CanM + CanR + CanSC

'

fit <- sem(model,data=data4,estimator='ML')

summary(fit,fit.measures=TRUE)

messages.subject: Re: categorical exogenous variables and significance
parts:
On 05/11/2016 04:35 PM, Kevin Ricks wrote:
> Given that canyon is an exogenous variable, from my understanding, I
> created 3 different dummy variables for the 4 canyons, populated by 0s
> and 1s, to delineate which canyon it is (like in classical regression).
> My first question is: is this the appropriate thing to do?

Yes. You need to do that yourself, and add the dummy variables to your
data.frame. Then, you can use them as any other predictor (just like
regression).

> Secondly, when building this model, I have all three canyon variables as
> factors controlling other variables. Below is the code for part of my
> base model. Right now I’m trying to trim down the model. From what I
> understand, I want to eliminate non-significant paths. However, with my
> categorical variables, what happens if two of the three are considered
> non-significant? Do I throw just those part of the canyon variable out
> of the model?

> In thinking back to classical regression, this doesn’t
> entirely feel right: rather, it seems like I should just keep them all
> in, unless they are all non-significant.

Indeed. This is identical to classic regression. You fit model with and
without those dummy's, and compare them using the anova() function.

Yves.
